subject: Request: temporary retention window and subprocessor evidence for Emerald Clinics
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@emeraldclinics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary retention window request + subprocessor evidence

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this — quick ask from our side. During our compliance review we identified a need for a short, temporary retention window for a small set of customer logs and backups related to an active investigation. We want to avoid immediate purging while our legal team completes a review and a third-party forensic scan.

Specifically we need:
- Ability to hold the named customer backups and application logs for an additional 90 days from today (emergency buffer).
- A statement of which subprocessors touch backups and an attestation of whether any subprocessor stores snapshots beyond your primary retention schedule.
- The expected backup purge timeline and any manual steps required for a forced purge once the buffer expires.

We understand this is an exception; we are happy to sign a short DPA addendum or access agreement if needed. Attached is a short spec with the items we need for audit.

Attachments: [attachment: Emerald_Request_Spec.pdf (pdf)]

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement — this is time sensitive for our client legal.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Legal Ops
Emerald Clinics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@emeraldclinics.com>
Cc: contracts@emeraldclinics.com
Date: 2026-05-08T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention window request + subprocessor evidence

Hi Marta — thanks, received.

Short answer: we can accommodate an emergency hold but I need to loop in Legal and Infrastructure for specifics. Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Legal will draft a short DPA addendum that defines the temporary buffer and the conditions for release/purge.
2) Infra will provide a per-customer snapshot list and the purge/playbook.
3) We will provide a subprocessor inventory and attestation (SOC2 where available).

Can you confirm the exact customer ID and the approximate number of snapshots/log buckets involved? That will help prioritization. We may be able to provision a 60-day buffer without escalation; 90 days will likely require the signed addendum.

I will follow up internally and get you a timeline by EOD.

– Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-05-08T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Emerald Clinics - temporary retention ask (need legal + ops input)

Kimberly / Aditya / Laura — forwarding an urgent request from Emerald Clinics (Marta Ruiz) below. Key asks: 90-day emergency hold for a small set of customer backups and logs, subprocessor inventory/attestation, and purge timeline + manual purge steps.

Internal notes / ask:
- Can Legal draft the minimal addendum language that authorizes a temporary retention buffer and limits scope (customer ID + object list)?
- Infra: can we produce the list of affected snapshots/buckets and the standard purge playbook? Also need confirmation whether any subprocessor retains backups beyond our retention (S3 replication partners, backup vendors).
- Ops (Laura): any risk to availability or billing if we isolate a small set of snapshots? What is the manual purge SLA once signoff is given?

Attachments we will provide back: redwood retention matrix (CSV), draft addendum. Please reply with proposed language or a short timeline. Marta asked for urgency — ideally same-day internal ack and a firm timeline within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@emeraldclinics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-05-08T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Emerald Clinics - temporary retention ask (need legal + ops input)

Jordan / team / Marta — thanks for the note. Quick legal position and proposed path:

1) Scope: we will accept a customer-specific, time-bound temporary hold limited to enumerated snapshots/log objects (must be supplied by Emerald).
2) Duration: 60 days can be granted at our discretion with a signed addendum; 90 days is exceptional and will require escalation to Legal leadership and a short justification from Emerald.
3) Required documents: signed DPA addendum, subprocessor inventory (CSV or spreadsheet), and a written confirmation from the customer that the data is being held for a named investigation.
4) Suggested addendum language (high-level):
   - Purpose clause: temporary retention for forensic review only; not for general backup extension.
   - Limitations: list of resources; expiry date; automatic purge procedure; customer indemnity for any extended storage costs.
   - Audit: Redwood to provide SOC2 report links and subprocessor attestations where available; otherwise a reasonable attestation from the subprocessor is acceptable.

Operational ask to Aditya/Laura: please provide the exact steps for isolating snapshots, the manual purge checklist, and an estimate of storage cost for a 60- and 90-day hold per 100GB. Also confirm if any of our backup subprocessors (replication partners, long-term archive vendors) may hold copies beyond Redwood control.

Marta — Jordan will coordinate the addendum and infra details. If you can provide the customer ID and the object names (or point us to them in your ticket), we can draft the addendum and a DocuSign link within 24 hours for 60-day holds.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@emeraldclinics.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Emerald Clinics - temporary retention ask (need legal + ops input)

Team / Marta — operational details below. Attaching the retention matrix and our purge playbook.

Summary: we can implement an isolated hold at the customer-object level. Two implementation options:
- Option A (fast): 60-day hold implemented within 24 hours. We mark snapshots with an "emergency_hold" tag and prevent scheduled purge jobs from touching them. Manual purge requires written signoff from Legal + customer.
- Option B (escalation): 90-day hold requires Legal signoff and a brief budget approval for additional storage; implementation timeline 48–72 hours because we need to route through long-term archive flags for replicated snapshots.

Purge steps (manual):
1) Validate signoff + DPA addendum in DocuSign.
2) Run the isolation verification script to confirm tag on each snapshot.
3) Notify backup vendor (if any) to remove replication flag.
4) Execute staged purge: move objects to short-term quarantine bucket for 24 hours, final delete after automated confirmation.

Subprocessor note: our primary backup subprocessor is CloudArch Partners; they replicate snapshots to their long-term store. CloudArch has confirmed they will honor Redwood retention tags provided we supply a signed addendum that includes explicit instruction. We can provide CloudArch's attestation PDF on request.

Attachments: [attachment: retention_matrix.csv (csv)], [attachment: backup-purge-playbook.md (md)], [attachment: CloudArch_Attestation.pdf (pdf) - available upon request]

Estimated incremental cost (per 100GB):
- 60-day hold: ~$4.30/day
- 90-day hold: ~$6.10/day (higher due to long-term replication flags)

We can proceed with Option A on receipt of the customer ID and object list. If Legal is comfortable with 90 days, we need the signed addendum first.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@emeraldclinics.com>, contracts@emeraldclinics.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention window request + subprocessor evidence

Marta — thank you for the patience. To move forward I can offer the following plan:

1) Short-term path (recommended): 60-day emergency hold implemented within 24 hours once you provide the customer ID and object list. Legal will require a signed DPA addendum (attached draft) that I will send via DocuSign.
2) Escalation path: 90-day hold is possible but requires additional justification from Emerald and Legal leadership signoff; Aditya noted extra replication cost.

Required from Emerald to start the 60-day hold:
- Customer ID: EMR-12897 (please confirm)
- List of snapshot IDs or S3 prefixes to hold
- Signed DPA addendum (DocuSign link below)

DocuSign for the draft addendum: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/emerald-dpa-addendum
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/emerald-clinics

If you confirm the ID and send the object list today we will: 1) implement Option A within 24 hours; 2) provide CloudArch attestation and our SOC2 summary; 3) provide the manual purge checklist and estimated incremental cost.

Next steps: please reply to confirm and we'll send the DocuSign request.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
